target.title: fix(agents): resolveMessagePrefix now checks channel and account messagePrefix configs
target.body:
@
## What Problem This Solves

The `resolveMessagePrefix` helper only checked the global `messages.messagePrefix` config, ignoring channel-specific and account-specific overrides. Operators could not set per-channel or per-account message prefixes, even though `ackReaction` and `responsePrefix` both correctly cascaded through all four levels.

## Root Cause

In `src/agents/identity.ts`, `resolveMessagePrefix` accepted `configured` and `hasAllowFrom` options but lacked the `channel` and `accountId` parameters that `resolveResponsePrefix` and `resolveAckReaction` already used. Additionally, `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` only passed `channel` + `accountId` to `resolveResponsePrefix`, not to `resolveMessagePrefix`.

## Changes

### Core fix ([src/agents/identity.ts](src/agents/identity.ts))

Implement the same L1–L4 precedence cascade used by `resolveResponsePrefix` and `resolveAckReaction`:

1. **L1**: Channel account level (`channels[X].accounts[Y].messagePrefix`)
2. **L2**: Channel level (`channels[X].messagePrefix`)
3. **L3**: Global messages level (`messages.messagePrefix`) or caller-configured option
4. **L4**: `hasAllowFrom` → identity name prefix → fallback (`"[openclaw]"`)

Also fixed `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` to pass `channel` + `accountId` through to `resolveMessagePrefix`.

### WhatsApp callers

- **message-line.ts**: Simplified from manually reading `cfg.channels?.whatsapp?.messagePrefix` via `configured` to passing `channel: "whatsapp"` — the function now resolves the cascade internally
- **message-line.runtime.ts**: Updated the WhatsApp runtime copy with the same L1–L4 cascade

### Tests

Added 25 new tests in `identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts` covering backward compatibility, channel-level, account-level, full cascade, and `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig` integration for messagePrefix resolution.

## Evidence

### Real behavior: vitest run (all 46 tests pass)

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > backward compatibility (no channel param) > returns fallback when no prefix configured anywhere 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > backward compatibility (no channel param) > returns global prefix when set 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > backward compatibility (no channel param) > returns empty string when global prefix is explicitly empty 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > backward compatibility (no channel param) > returns empty string when hasAllowFrom is true and no prefix configured 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > backward compatibility (no channel param) > returns identity name prefix when configured and identity has name 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > channel-level prefix > returns channel prefix when set, ignoring global 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > channel-level prefix > falls through to global when channel prefix is undefined 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > channel-level prefix > channel empty string stops cascade (no global prefix applied) 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > channel-level prefix > different channels get different prefixes 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > channel-level prefix > falls through to fallback when channel not in config 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > account-level prefix > returns account prefix when set, ignoring channel and global 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > account-level prefix > falls through to channel prefix when account prefix is undefined 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > account-level prefix > falls through to global when both account and channel are undefined 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > account-level prefix > account empty string stops cascade 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > account-level prefix > different accounts on same channel get different prefixes 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > account-level prefix > unknown accountId falls through to channel level 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > full cascade > L1: account prefix wins when all levels set 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > full cascade > L2: channel prefix when account undefined 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > full cascade > L3: global prefix when channel has no prefix 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > full cascade > L4: identity name fallback when no prefix at any level 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig with channel context > passes channel context through to messagePrefix resolution 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig with channel context > uses global when no channel context provided 0ms
 ✓ |unit-fast| .../identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts > resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override > resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig with channel context > passes accountId context through to messagePrefix resolution 0ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
   Duration  1.56s
```

### Static verification: cascade is structurally identical to resolveResponsePrefix

The fix uses the same `getChannelConfig` helper and the same L1→L2→L3→L4 cascade structure already used by `resolveResponsePrefix` and `resolveAckReaction`. Each level returns `undefined` to fall through to the next, and empty string is treated as an explicit "no prefix" that stops the cascade — exactly matching the existing pattern.

Fixes #102937
